title: Arcadia Tenebra - A look at the protoype
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xtwXWyEfhk

Daniel (@dungeondive) looks at a prototype of Arcadia Tenebra ahead of its second Kickstarter attempt, the first having failed to fund. His pitch: if you like A Touch of Evil, this lives in that space with little overlap.

You play anti-heroes in an Eastern European, folklore-and-steampunk province — Nikola Tesla among the cast — racing to gather three clues and return them to the police chief before the blood moon rises. The murder mystery is a backdrop, not a deduction puzzle; you solve it by adventuring. Each region offers a choice of charisma, intelligence or combat encounter, and a midgame border crossing flips the bestiary from mundane to supernatural.

What he singles out are the lucky and unlucky decks. Some cards are events, some are items that arrive attached to a small quest you must complete before equipping them, and cursed unluckies come with their own removal quest that can drag you somewhere you'd never have gone. He calls this an element he wishes more games had. The shop restocking from other players' discards also earns a nod.

The concerns are candid: the game feels too easy with nothing to waylay you between regions, the rulebook is long, poorly organised and shows translation strain, and the encounter decks are thin. He pins his hopes on two announced systems, tasks and investigations.

----

Does a mystery still work as a backdrop if the game gives you no way to actually solve it?
